Subject: Questions on SOC2, pen test and evidence cadence for order form

Jordan —

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement here wants to lock language for the security exhibit in the MSA/order form before we run signatures. A few quick items we need clarity on so our legal and infosec teams can greenlight: 

- SOC 2: we need confirmation on the timing (annual attestation only? interim reports? how soon after signature we can expect the most recent report).
- Pen test: will Redwood allow a coordinated third-party test against staging? If yes, what notice and access windows do you require and what access (read-only/staging creds)?
- Audit rights / inspection: our compliance lead is pushing for a limited inspection right (samples only) — can you confirm proposed guardrails and evidence cadence (monthly snapshots, query extracts, log retention windows)?

I've attached a short RFP sheet with our standard questions. Can you send an initial redline suggestion for the security exhibit (MSA Appendix) and a short schedule for how evidence will be shared? We prefer a redline we can comment on directly.

Proposed timeline from our side: order form signed by 10/20, SOC/pen-test items agreed by 10/10. Is that achievable?

Thanks —
Sarah Lee
Senior Procurement Manager
Nova Medical

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@novamed.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Oct 2028 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on SOC2, pen test and evidence cadence for order form

Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (Legal) and Marcus (Infra) to capture legal and operational constraints; copying Derek as well. I put together an initial draft of exhibit redlines and an operational summary below. Draft redline attached for your team to comment on.

High-level proposal (summary):
- SOC 2: Redwood will provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II attestation (covering the inference platform and control environment) within 10 business days of request; annual external attestation to be provided within 30 days of publication. We can also provide a read-only SOC 2 report portal link to customers under NDA.
- Pen test: We accept coordinated third-party penetration tests against a customer-specific staging environment under the following guardrails: 30-day advance notice, mutually agreeable 7-calendar-day testing window (single contiguous week preferred), scoped IP ranges and time-limited staging credentials, and a single point-of-contact on both sides. Redwood requires final report delivery to include remediation timeline requests and will work with customers on mitigation plans.
- Audit/inspection rights: Redwood proposes "bounded inspection" language — sample-based evidence requests limited to relevant application logs and configuration snapshots for the period in-scope, requested no more than once per quarter except during incident investigations. Requests must be submitted 30 days in advance and will include a data minimization requirement. On-site privileged access is explicitly excluded; remote read-only evidence transfer is supported.
- Evidence cadence: we can support monthly automated snapshots for agreed metrics (token logs, API call volume, error rates) plus quarterly attestations. Raw customer payloads are not accessible to Redwood personnel without explicit authorization (we preserve customer privacy by design).

Open items for legal: specifics on retention windows (we typically retain operational logs 90 days hot, 3 years archived), and whether Nova requires any raw payload access that would change scope.

Next steps we propose:
1) Laura to provide contract redline comments in tracked changes (legal).
2) Marcus to draft a short ops runbook describing the staging access flow + pen test requester checklist (technical).
3) Joint 30-minute call with Nova legal/infosec next week to confirm.

Can you confirm whether the 10/10 internal agreement date is firm? If so we will prioritize.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_draft_security_exhibit_redlines.docx (docx)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@novamed.com>, Derek Chu <derek.chu@novamed.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Oct 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Questions on SOC2, pen test and evidence cadence for order form

Folks — I reviewed Jordan's draft and made targeted redlines. Key legal positions below (see attached markup):

- Bounded inspection: keep, but clarify definition of "sample" (max 5% of records per request or a fixed sample set agreed in advance). We recommend limiting inspection frequency to once per 12 months for routine audits, with an exception path for incident-driven requests.
- Notice & scope: 30 calendar days notice for pen-test and for inspection requests; pen-test scope must be agreed in writing and Redwood will provide a staging environment with obfuscated data.
- SOC 2 access: provide a certified SOC 2 Type II report annually. If Nova requires more frequent evidence, they must accept a mutual NDA addendum and pay for any additional on-demand compliance work.
- Data handling: call out that Redwood will not provide raw customer payloads except under a court order or explicit customer instruction. Add a clause requiring customers to redact PHI from artifacts submitted for testing unless a HIPAA BA is in place.

Contractual redlines I added: explicit limits on the scope of inspection, indemnity carveouts for issues caused by customer misconfiguration, and a requirement that third-party testers sign Redwood's tester agreement (we'll prepare a standard).

Please note: the negotiating point is frequency and scope; if Nova insists on monthly unbounded evidence pulls we will need to evaluate operational impact and likely push for an additional professional services fee.

I recommend we offer a compromise: quarterly evidence snapshots + one annual inspection right (sample-based) with an option for an expedited ad-hoc inspection subject to fees and a higher notice period. Marcus, please confirm the feasibility of monthly automated snapshots and the proposed log retention (90 days hot, 3 years archive).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

Thanks all — this is helpful. A few clarifications from Nova's side: 

- We can accept the annual SOC 2 deliverable as the baseline. We still need access to the most recent report prior to signature (Nova security team requires it to close procurement). 10 business days from request is acceptable.
- Pen test: 30-day notice and a single-week window is workable. Nova will ensure our testers sign Redwood's tester agreement; please share that. We do need the staging environment to mirror production configs as closely as possible (with obfuscated PHI) — Marcus, what's the best way to coordinate on data obfuscation?
- Evidence cadence: quarterly snapshots + one annual sample inspection is a fine compromise. We request that Redwood include a short runbook in the order form (appendix) that describes how and where snapshots are delivered (S3 link or secure portal) and the expected SLA for evidence delivery (e.g., 5 business days).

If we can get the SOC 2 report and the tester agreement by Monday (10/8), Nova will meet the 10/10 internal deadline. Also propose a 30-minute technical sync Monday 10/9 11:00 AM ET to walk through staging access steps.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Derek Chu
Director, IT Security — Nova Medical
